docs.title: Coffee Capsule Production Optimizer Agent
docs.text:
An agentic Business Intelligence application for a coffee-capsule production plant. It analyses sensor data, quantifies inefficiencies in €, and generates a production plan.

  • Getting Started

    Install, build the DuckDB warehouse, and launch the dashboard in minutes.

    Quick start

  • Architecture

    Parquet lake → DuckDB warehouse → Streamlit dashboard → Agent.

    Architecture

  • Analytics

    A library of 19 self-documenting analytical SQL queries.

    Analytics

  • Agent

    A tool-using agent that diagnoses, quantifies and plans — fully offline, with an optional LLM narrative.

    Agent

docs.title: The business problem
docs.text:
Coffee-capsule plants run high-speed, multi-stage lines where small losses — micro-stops, slow changeovers, rejects, energy waste, unplanned failures — compound into significant cost. The data to see these losses exists (minute-level sensor readings), but turning it into decisions requires analytics, domain logic and planning.

This project closes that loop:

flowchart LR
    A[Sensor data] --> B[Analytics<br/>OEE · downtime · quality · energy]
    B --> C[Diagnosis<br/>inefficiencies in €]
    C --> D[Production plan<br/>& schedule]
    D --> E[Executive narrative]

docs.title: The dataset at a glance
docs.text: Item Value Production lines 3 Machines 51 Sensor granularity 1 minute Period One full year Volume ~26.8 M rows (Parquet) Nature Synthetic

docs.title: Tech stack
docs.text:
Layer Technology Storage Parquet data lake Warehouse / query engine DuckDB Analytics SQL (views, aggregates, gaps-and-islands fact tables) UI Streamlit + Plotly Agent Python, deterministic engine + optional LLM

Two ways to use it

  • Explore — use the Streamlit dashboard to browse KPIs, Pareto charts, heatmaps and run SQL.
  • Decide — run the agent to get a diagnosis, a plan and a reasoning trace.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Do I need an LLM to run the agent?

No. The agent runs fully offline. An LLM only adds an executive narrative.

Is the data real?

No — it is a synthetic dataset of a coffee-capsule plant.

Where does the warehouse live?

In a local DuckDB file, coffee_bi.duckdb, created by scripts/init_db.py.

The app can't find the dataset.

Set COFFEE_DATA_DIR to the dataset folder. See Configuration.

How do I add a new metric?

Add a .sql file to sql/analytics/, then expose it in the dashboard and/or as an agent tool.

How do I preview these docs locally? 

pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs serve
Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000.

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
A tool-using agent that analyses the sensor data, quantifies inefficiencies in €, and generates a production plan.

flowchart LR
    T[Tools<br/>query warehouse] --> AN[Analyzers<br/>find & cost losses]
    AN --> PL[Planner + Optimizer<br/>build plan & schedule]
    PL --> RP[Report<br/>markdown outputs]
    RP -. optional .-> LLM[LLM<br/>executive narrative]

docs.text: Property Detail Offline by default Runs fully on a deterministic engine — reproducible results LLM-optional If credentials are present, adds an executive narrative Explainable Produces a reasoning trace alongside the plan Two interfaces CLI (python -m agent.run_agent) and the dashboard Agent tab

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: python -m agent.run_agent [options]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# 28-day plan, automatic narrative (if LLM available)
python -m agent.run_agent

# Custom horizon and demand growth
python -m agent.run_agent --horizon 42 --growth 1.10

# Explicit demand per product family, no LLM
python -m agent.run_agent --demand STRONG=4e7,MILD=3e7,DECAF=2.5e7 --no-llm

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Description --horizon N Planning horizon in days (default 28) --growth F Demand growth multiplier, e.g. 1.10 = +10% --demand K=V,... Explicit demand per product family --no-llm Skip the LLM narrative

Run python -m agent.run_agent --help for the full list.

docs.title: LLM Narrative
docs.text:
The LLM is optional. All numbers, diagnoses and plans come from the deterministic engine; the LLM only writes an executive narrative on top.

Mode Behaviour No credentials / --no-llm Deterministic outputs only Credentials present Deterministic outputs + executive narrative

docs.title: Why this design
docs.text:
• Reproducible — same inputs, same plan.
  • Trustworthy — the LLM cannot alter computed figures.
  • Runs anywhere — works offline for demos and testing.

Configure credentials via environment variables (see agent/llm.py for the exact names).

docs.title: Agent Modules
docs.text:
Module Role agent/agent.py Orchestrates the run: tools → analysis → planning → reporting agent/tools.py Tools the agent calls to retrieve metrics from DuckDB agent/analyzers.py Detects inefficiencies and quantifies them in € agent/planner.py Builds the production plan from demand and capacity agent/optimizer.py Optimisation model used by the planner agent/report.py Generates markdown outputs agent/llm.py Optional LLM client for the executive narrative agent/run_agent.py Command-line entry point

Extending the agent

To add a new capability: write the SQL in sql/analytics/, expose it as a tool in tools.py, consume it in analyzers.py, and surface it in report.py.

docs.title: Production Optimizer
docs.text: The optimizer (agent/optimizer.py) turns demand and plant capability into a production plan.

docs.title: Problem framing
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph Inputs
        D[Demand per product]
        C[Line capacity<br/>from observed OEE]
        K[Costs<br/>energy · changeovers · rejects]
        M[Maintenance risk]
    end
    Inputs --> O[Optimisation model]
    O --> P[Plan: volume per line × product × period]
    O --> S[Schedule]

docs.title: Conceptual formulation
docs.text:
Decision variables — how much of each product to make on each line in each period.

Objective — minimise total cost (or maximise value) of meeting demand:

\[ \min \sum_{l,p,t} c_{l,p}\, x_{l,p,t} \;+\; \text{changeover costs} \;+\; \text{penalties} \]

Constraints (typical)

  • Demand coverage over the horizon
  • Line capacity per period, based on realistic (observed) performance
  • Product–line compatibility
  • Changeover and maintenance considerations

Note

This page describes the model conceptually. See agent/optimizer.py for the exact variables, constraints, objective and solver used.

docs.title: Why it matters
docs.text: Using observed OEE rather than nameplate capacity makes the plan feasible in practice — the optimizer plans for the plant as it really performs, while the diagnosis shows how much capacity could be recovered.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
The agent writes its results to agent_output/, including efficiency_report.md.

Output Content Efficiency report Diagnosis of inefficiencies, quantified in € Production plan Volumes per line and product over the horizon Schedule Time-phased schedule Reasoning trace Steps and tool calls the agent made Executive narrative Optional, LLM-generated summary

The same outputs are visible in the dashboard's Agent tab.

docs.title: Agent Workflow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    S([Start]) --> I[Read inputs<br/>horizon · demand · growth]
    I --> Q[Call tools<br/>pull metrics from DuckDB]
    Q --> D[Diagnose<br/>OEE losses, downtime, rejects,<br/>changeovers, energy, maintenance risk]
    D --> E[Quantify impact in €]
    E --> P[Plan production<br/>allocate demand across lines & products]
    P --> SC[Build schedule]
    SC --> R[Write report & reasoning trace]
    R --> L{LLM credentials?}
    L -- yes --> N[Add executive narrative]
    L -- no --> O([Done])
    N --> O

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Inputs — planning horizon (default 28 days), demand per product family or a growth factor.
  2. Tools — the agent calls tools (tools.py) that query the warehouse.
  3. Diagnosis — analyzers (analyzers.py) identify where capacity and money are lost.
  4. Quantification — each inefficiency is expressed in €, so priorities are comparable.
  5. Planning — the planner (planner.py) and optimizer (optimizer.py) produce a plan that meets demand.
  6. Reporting — report.py writes the efficiency report, plan, schedule and trace.
  7. Narrative (optional) — llm.py summarises the result for executives.

docs.title: Analytics Library
docs.text: sql/analytics/ contains 19 self-documenting analytical queries. They are the single source of truth for metrics shown in the dashboard and used by the agent.

docs.title: Coverage
docs.text: Area Examples of questions answered OEE & performance Line / machine OEE; availability, performance, quality; bottlenecks; rolling 7-day OEE Reliability & downtime Downtime Pareto with cumulative %; MTBF vs MTTR Quality & output Output by product; yield; worst offenders; changeover matrix Energy & cost Daily cost; kWh per 1,000 capsules; energy by product Predictive maintenance Risk ranking; vibration exceedance; degradation ↔ reject correlation; temperature anomalies; maintenance schedule Utilisation State-utilisation stack; hour × weekday heatmap

docs.title: Running a query
docs.text:
From the dashboard, open SQL Explorer, pick a saved query or write your own, and download results as CSV.

Self-documenting

Each .sql file carries a header comment describing what it computes — open the file for the exact logic.

See KPI Definitions.

docs.title: KPI Definitions
docs.text: Standard manufacturing definitions used throughout the project. Refer to the SQL files for the exact implementation.

docs.title: OEE
docs.text: \[ \text{OEE} = \text{Availability} \times \text{Performance} \times \text{Quality} \] Component Definition Availability Run time ÷ planned production time Performance (Ideal cycle time × total count) ÷ run time Quality Good count ÷ total count

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text: \[ \text{MTBF} = \frac{\text{Operating time}}{\text{Number of failures}} \qquad \text{MTTR} = \frac{\text{Total repair time}}{\text{Number of repairs}} \]

docs.title: Energy intensity
docs.text: \[ \text{kWh per 1{,}000 capsules} = \frac{\text{kWh}}{\text{capsules produced}} \times 1000 \]

docs.title: Yield
docs.text: \[ \text{Yield} = \frac{\text{Good capsules}}{\text{Total capsules}} \]

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The solution is self-contained: no external database server and no cloud dependency for the core analytics or the agent's deterministic engine.

flowchart LR
    subgraph Lake["Parquet lake"]
        P1[sensor data]
        P2[machine master]
        P3[products]
        P4[schedule]
    end

    subgraph WH["DuckDB warehouse (coffee_bi.duckdb)"]
        V[Raw views<br/>01_raw_views.sql]
        AGG[Aggregates & fact tables<br/>02_build_aggregates.sql]
        Q[19 analytics queries<br/>sql/analytics/*.sql]
    end

    subgraph App["Applications"]
        DB[app/db.py<br/>access layer]
        UI[Streamlit + Plotly<br/>app/dashboard.py]
        AG[Agent<br/>agent/]
    end

    Lake --> V --> AGG --> Q
    Q --> DB --> UI
    DB --> AG
    AG --> UI
    AG -. optional .-> LLM[(LLM)]

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text: Principle How it shows up Query in place DuckDB reads Parquet directly through views — no ETL copy. Pay once for heavy work Expensive roll-ups are materialised once into compact tables. SQL as a library Analytics are versioned, self-documenting .sql files reused by UI and agent. Deterministic first The agent's analysis and plan don't depend on an LLM. LLM as narrator When available, the LLM explains — it does not compute.

docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant L as Parquet lake
    participant I as scripts/init_db.py
    participant D as DuckDB
    participant U as Dashboard
    participant A as Agent

    I->>D: create raw views over Parquet
    I->>D: build aggregates & fact tables
    U->>D: run analytics queries
    D-->>U: KPIs, trends, Pareto, heatmaps
    A->>D: call analysis tools
    D-->>A: metrics
    A->>A: diagnose → quantify € → plan

docs.title: Stages
docs.text:
1. Ingest (virtual) — sql/01_raw_views.sql exposes raw_sensor, dim_machine, dim_product, raw_schedule.
  2. Aggregate — sql/02_build_aggregates.sql produces hourly/daily roll-ups and episode-level fact tables.
  3. Analyse — sql/analytics/*.sql compute OEE, downtime, quality, energy and maintenance metrics.
  4. Consume — the dashboard visualises; the agent reasons and plans.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
The synthetic plant dataset models 3 production lines and 51 machines, with 1-minute sensor readings over a full year (~26.8 M rows in Parquet).

The warehouse is built in two layers:

Layer File Purpose Raw views sql/01_raw_views.sql Zero-copy views over Parquet Aggregates & facts sql/02_build_aggregates.sql One-time heavy roll-ups into compact tables
  • Raw Views
  • Aggregates & Fact Tables

docs.title: Aggregates & Fact Tables
docs.text:
Defined in sql/02_build_aggregates.sql. Heavy computations run once and are stored as compact tables, so dashboards and the agent stay fast.

Table Grain Used for agg_machine_hour machine × hour Intraday patterns, heatmaps agg_machine_day machine × day Trends, OEE, reliability agg_line_product_day line × product × day Output, yield, energy by product fact_downtime_episode one row per downtime episode Pareto, MTBF / MTTR fact_changeover_episode one row per changeover Changeover matrix & losses

docs.title: Gaps-and-islands
docs.text:
Downtime and changeover episodes are derived from minute-level states using the gaps-and-islands pattern: consecutive minutes in the same state are collapsed into a single episode with a start, end and duration.

flowchart LR
    A["RUN RUN DOWN DOWN DOWN RUN"] --> B["episode: DOWN, 3 min"]

docs.title: Raw Views
docs.text:
Defined in sql/01_raw_views.sql. These are views, not tables — DuckDB reads the Parquet files on demand, so nothing is duplicated.

View Description raw_sensor Minute-level sensor readings per machine dim_machine Machine master data dim_product Product master data raw_schedule Production schedule 
-- example: readings for one machine
SELECT *
FROM raw_sensor
WHERE machine_id = '<machine_id>'
LIMIT 100;

docs.title: Suggested demo script (≈5 minutes)
docs.text: # Step Message 1 Overview tab "A year of minute-level data from 51 machines — here's how the plant performs." 2 Reliability & Downtime "A few causes explain most downtime — the Pareto makes it obvious." 3 Predictive Maintenance "We can see which machines are degrading before they fail." 4 Agent tab → Run "Now the agent does the analyst's job: diagnose, quantify in €, plan." 5 Plan & trace "A feasible plan, with a transparent reasoning trace." 6 Narrative "And an executive summary — numbers stay deterministic."

docs.title: Key messages
docs.text:
• From data to decisions: analytics → € impact → plan.
  • Deterministic core, LLM as narrator — trustworthy and reproducible.
  • Self-contained — DuckDB + Parquet, no infrastructure needed.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Up and running in three commands:

pip install -r requirements.txt
python scripts/init_db.py          # build coffee_bi.duckdb (one-time)
streamlit run app/dashboard.py     # open the UI

Then, to run the agent from the command line:

python -m agent.run_agent
Step Page 1. Install dependencies Installation 2. Point to the dataset Configuration 3. Build the warehouse & run Running the App

docs.title: Dataset location
docs.text:
By default the app looks for the dataset in ../coffee_capsule_dataset. If it lives elsewhere, set COFFEE_DATA_DIR:

Windows (PowerShell)macOS / Linux 
$env:COFFEE_DATA_DIR = "C:\path\to\coffee_capsule_dataset"

export COFFEE_DATA_DIR="/path/to/coffee_capsule_dataset"

Central settings live in config.py.

docs.title: Optional: LLM credentials
docs.text:
The agent runs fully offline on its deterministic engine. If LLM credentials are available, it additionally produces an executive narrative. See LLM Narrative.

Secrets

Never commit credentials. Keep them in environment variables or a local .env file that is listed in .gitignore.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10+ (recommended)
  • Git
  • The synthetic coffee-capsule dataset in Parquet format

docs.title: Clone the repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/mmbellani/coffee-capsules-production-optimizer-agent.git
cd coffee-capsules-production-optimizer-agent

docs.title: Create a virtual environment
docs.text:
Windows (PowerShell)macOS / Linux 
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

docs.title: Install dependencies
docs.text: pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: 1. Build the warehouse
docs.text:
python scripts/init_db.py

This creates coffee_bi.duckdb by:

  1. Creating views over the Parquet files (sql/01_raw_views.sql) — no data copy.
  2. Materialising compact aggregates and fact tables (sql/02_build_aggregates.sql).

It is a one-time step and takes seconds.

docs.title: 2. Launch the dashboard
docs.text:
streamlit run app/dashboard.py

Streamlit opens the UI in your browser. See Dashboard for a tour.

docs.title: 3. Run the agent
docs.text:
python -m agent.run_agent

Outputs are written to agent_output/. See CLI Reference and Outputs.
